sts1.title: File:STS-1 File Footage for 40th Anniversary.webm
sts1.author: NASA
sts1.credit: NASA Image and Video Library
sts1.desc: The Space Shuttle Columbia began a new era of manned spaceflight when it lifted off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center on STS-1, the inaugural flight in the Space Shuttle Program on April 12, 1981. Aboard the spacecraft were astronauts John W. Young, commander, and Robert L. Crippen, pilot.

guncam.title: File:Shuttle Columbia Disaster gun camera footage.webm
guncam.credit: YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lNfEUkxmliQ – View/save a
guncam.desc: On Feb. 1, 2003, two Dutch[1] pilots were training on an AH-64D Longbow Apache helicopter out of Fort Hood, Texas when they witnessed and recorded with the attack helicopter’s onboard camera the Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrating on its way back to Kennedy Space Center at the end of the STS-107 mission. mct.author: NASA
mct.desc: Side-by-Side edit of post-CAIB telemetry data examination and NASA in-house videography of mission control on February 1st 2003 STS-107 mission that resulted in the loss of the Space Shuttle Columbia and all 7 crew members. Copyrighted-portions of this film have been removed to maintain NASA Public-Domain status.
